title: Reductivity detected by codimension-one torus centralizers
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], and let $H$ be a smooth connected affine $k$-group scheme of finite type [def-sc-group-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Closed subgroup schemes are as in [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. A torus is a closed subgroup isomorphic to $\mathbf G_m^r$ for some $r\geq0$, with $\mathbf G_m(A)=A^\times$; maximal means maximal among these subgroups. A smooth affine group is unipotent if all its geometric points in a faithful finite-dimensional matrix representation satisfy $(u-I)^n=0$ for some $n\geq1$. Reductive means having no nontrivial smooth connected normal unipotent closed subgroup. Let $T\subseteq H$ be a maximal torus with scheme-theoretic centralizer $C_H(T)=T$. Here $C_H(K)(A)$ consists of elements commuting with $K(A')$ after every commutative $A$-algebra extension $A'$. Put $X=\operatorname{Hom}(T,\mathbf G_m)$ and let $\Psi\subseteq X\setminus\{0\}$ be the nonzero character weights of the conjugation action of $T$ on $\operatorname{Lie}(H)$, the tangent space at the identity [def-sc-scheme-tangent-space]. For $\alpha\in\Psi$, put $L_\alpha=X\cap\mathbf Q\alpha$ and $T_\alpha=\operatorname{Spec}k[X/L_\alpha]\subseteq T=\operatorname{Spec}k[X]$, where $k[M]$ is the group algebra with basis $e^m$ and multiplication $e^me^n=e^{m+n}$. Thus $T_\alpha$ is the largest torus in $\ker\alpha$ and has codimension one. Then $H$ is reductive if and only if $C_H(T_\alpha)$ is reductive for every $\alpha\in\Psi$. This includes $\Psi=\varnothing$. All weights are torus characters; there is no restriction on characteristic.

source.place: WANTED locally; read online https://math.stanford.edu/~conrad/papers/luminysga3smf.pdf . Lemma 3.1.10, printed p.87, full statement, including empty nonzero-weight set; torus kernels are defined by the saturated character subgroup, not by their possibly nonreduced scheme-theoretic identity components.

proof.text: First check the subtori in the statement. Choose $T\simeq\mathbf G_m^r$. Characters correspond to the group-like Laurent monomials by [lem-sfb-group-algebra-group-like-basis], so $X\simeq\mathbf Z^r$. For nonzero $\alpha$, $L_\alpha=X\cap\mathbf Q\alpha$ is a rank-one saturated subgroup: $nx\in L_\alpha$, $n\ne0$, implies $x\in\mathbf Q\alpha$. Thus $X/L_\alpha$ is finitely generated torsion-free, and is free by [lem-trf-fg-torsionfree-group-free]; its rank is $r-1$ by tensoring with $\mathbf Q$. The quotient of group algebras defines the displayed closed inclusion, and [lem-sfb-diagonalizable-group-geometric-criteria] makes $T_\alpha$ a split torus of rank $r-1$. The restriction of $\alpha$ is zero since $\alpha\in L_\alpha$. If a torus $S\subseteq\ker\alpha$ is given, every $x\in L_\alpha$ has $nx=m\alpha$ for some $n>0$; its restriction to $S$ is torsion, hence zero since the character group of a split torus is free. Therefore $S$ factors through $T_\alpha$, verifying the largest-torus assertion. If $H$ is reductive, apply [lem-sfb-reductive-torus-fixed-subgroup] to each $T_\alpha\subseteq H$. It gives exactly the required reductivity of $C_H(T_\alpha)$.

source.place: Agent assembly of the torus weight argument of Conrad, Lemma 3.1.10, printed p.87 (online; local copy WANTED), using Milne 10.12--10.21, 13.1, 17.59. The identity-component variation below avoids assuming connectedness of a fixed subgroup.

proof.text: For the converse assume every $C_H(T_\alpha)$ is reductive. Let $N\subseteq H$ be an arbitrary smooth connected normal unipotent closed subgroup; it suffices to prove $N=1$. Write $\mathfrak h=\operatorname{Lie}(H)$, $\mathfrak n=\operatorname{Lie}(N)$, and use the bijections $E_{H,R}:\mathfrak h\otimes_kR\to\ker(H(R[\delta])\to H(R))$ and the representation $\operatorname{Ad}_H:H\to\operatorname{GL}(\mathfrak h)$ of [lem-sfb-affine-group-dual-number-calculus]; the conjugation action of $T$ on $\mathfrak h$ in the statement is $\operatorname{Ad}_H|_T$. By its closed-subgroup clause, $\mathrm di:\mathfrak n\to\mathfrak h$ is injective and $E_{H,R}$ maps $\mathfrak n\otimes_kR$ onto $N(R[\delta])\cap\ker(H(R[\delta])\to H(R))$. For $t\in T(R)$ and $u\in\mathfrak n\otimes_kR$, normality [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup] over the algebra $R[\delta]$ gives $tE_{H,R}(u)t^{-1}\in N(R[\delta])$, and this element still reduces to $e$; hence $\operatorname{Ad}_H(t)u\in\mathfrak n\otimes_kR$, and likewise for $t^{-1}$. Thus $t\mapsto\operatorname{Ad}_H(t)|_{\mathfrak n\otimes_kR}$ is a family of group homomorphisms $T(R)\to\operatorname{GL}(\mathfrak n)(R)$, natural in $R$, hence (Yoneda on affine $k$-schemes) a homomorphism of $k$-group schemes $\rho:T\to\operatorname{GL}(\mathfrak n)$ for which $\mathrm di$ is equivariant. Apply [lem-sfb-split-torus-representation-weight-decomposition] to $(\mathfrak n,\rho)$: it is the direct sum of its character weight spaces $\mathfrak n_\chi$. Equivariance and injectivity of $\mathrm di\otimes_kR$ give $\mathfrak n_\chi\subseteq\mathfrak h_\chi$. In particular any nonzero $\chi$ for which $\mathfrak n_\chi\ne0$ belongs to the set $\Psi$ of the statement.

source.place: Agent assembly of the torus weight argument of Conrad, Lemma 3.1.10, printed p.87 (online; local copy WANTED), using Milne 10.12--10.21, 13.1, 17.59. The identity-component variation below avoids assuming connectedness of a fixed subgroup.

proof.text: For any subtorus $S\subseteq T$, put $C_S=C_H(S)$ and $W_S=N\times_H C_S$. The centralizer theorem [lem-sfb-torus-centralizer-smooth-connected] (here $\bar k=k$, so connected is geometrically connected) makes $C_S$ a smooth connected closed subgroup representing the centralizer functor. The fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product] is a closed subgroup of $N$ and of $H$; on affine coordinate rings it is a quotient of $k[N]$, hence is affine of finite type. Its points are $W_S(A)=N(A)\cap C_S(A)$: exactly the elements of $N$ fixed by conjugation by $S$ after every algebra extension. Apply [lem-sfb-torus-fixed-scheme-smooth] with $X=N$, the action $S\times N\to N$ restricted from conjugation by normality of $N$, and $F=W_S$; $N$ is smooth affine of finite type, so $W_S$ is smooth. For the tangent space, [lem-sfb-lie-normalizer-centralizer-invariants] with $G=H$, $K=S$, $C=C_S$ gives $\operatorname{Lie}(C_S)=\mathfrak h^S$ inside $\mathfrak h$. The closed-subgroup clause of [lem-sfb-affine-group-dual-number-calculus] with $R=k$, applied to $W_S$, $N$ and $C_S$ inside $H$, identifies each tangent space with the points of $H(k[\delta])$ over $e$ that lie in the subgroup; since $W_S(k[\delta])=N(k[\delta])\cap C_S(k[\delta])$, $\operatorname{Lie}(W_S)=\mathfrak n\cap\mathfrak h^S$. As $\rho$ of step 2 is the restriction of $\operatorname{Ad}_H$ and $\mathrm di\otimes_kR$ is injective, $\mathfrak n\cap\mathfrak h^S=\mathfrak n^S$, the vectors $v$ with $\rho_R(s)(v\otimes1)=v\otimes1$ for all $R$ and $s\in S(R)$. These equalities concern the full fixed functor on nonreduced test algebras.

source.place: Agent assembly of the torus weight argument of Conrad, Lemma 3.1.10, printed p.87 (online; local copy WANTED), using Milne 10.12--10.21, 13.1, 17.59. The identity-component variation below avoids assuming connectedness of a fixed subgroup.

proof.text: Fix $\alpha\in\Psi$ and take $S=T_\alpha$. Let $M_\alpha=W_S^0$. By [lem-sfb-finite-type-group-identity-subgroup], this is a connected open and closed subgroup of $W_S$, in particular closed in $C_S$ and of finite type. It is smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-restrict-open-subschemes]. It is unipotent: restricting a faithful matrix representation of $N$ to this closed subgroup is still faithful, and every geometric matrix remains unipotent. For $c\in C_S(k)$, conjugation preserves $N$ by normality, and preserves $C_S$ because $c$ commutes with $S$; consequently it preserves $W_S$ as a subgroup scheme. It fixes the identity, so it preserves the connected component $M_\alpha$ with its open-subscheme structure. As $C_S$ is smooth, [lem-sfb-smooth-ambient-normality-geometric] makes $M_\alpha$ normal in $C_S$. Reductivity of $C_S$, which is the converse hypothesis for this $\alpha$, now gives $M_\alpha=1$. Since $M_\alpha\hookrightarrow W_S$ is open and contains the identity, every dual-number tangent vector at the identity factors through it (its underlying space has one point). Thus $\operatorname{Lie}(W_S)=\operatorname{Lie}(M_\alpha)=0$ by [def-sc-scheme-tangent-space]. Combined with step 3, $\mathfrak n^{T_\alpha}=0$.

proof.text: If $v\in\mathfrak n_\alpha$ with $\alpha\in\Psi$, then every $t\in T_\alpha(R)$ acts on $v\otimes1$ by the scalar $\alpha_R(t)=1$. Hence $\mathfrak n_\alpha\subseteq\mathfrak n^{T_\alpha}=0$ by step 4. Step 2 says these are all possible nonzero character weights of $\mathfrak n$. Its direct-sum decomposition therefore gives $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak n_0=\mathfrak n^T$. If $\Psi$ is empty the same conclusion follows immediately from step 2; no choice of a character was made.

source.place: Agent assembly of the torus weight argument of Conrad, Lemma 3.1.10, printed p.87 (online; local copy WANTED), using Milne 10.12--10.21, 13.1, 17.59. The identity-component variation below avoids assuming connectedness of a fixed subgroup.

proof.text: Take $S=T$ in step 3 and let $M=W_T^0$. The identity-component result [lem-sfb-finite-type-group-identity-subgroup] and smooth restriction [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-restrict-open-subschemes] show that $M$ is a smooth connected closed subgroup of $N$. It is unipotent by restriction of the same faithful representation. The assumed scheme-theoretic equality $C_H(T)=T$ identifies $W_T$ with $N\times_H T$, so $M\hookrightarrow H$ factors as a closed subgroup inclusion $M\hookrightarrow T$. Apply [lem-sfb-unipotent-to-multiplicative-trivial] to this homomorphism: the source is unipotent and the target is a torus, hence of multiplicative type. It is the trivial homomorphism, and is a monomorphism, so $M=1$. The open immersion $M\hookrightarrow W_T$ induces an equality of tangent spaces at the identity, by the dual-number factorization just used in step 4 [def-sc-scheme-tangent-space]. Consequently step 3 gives $\mathfrak n^T=\operatorname{Lie}(W_T)=\operatorname{Lie}(M)=0$.

proof.text: Steps 5 and 6 give $\operatorname{Lie}(N)=T_{N/k,e}=0$. Since $\kappa(e)=k$, [lem-sc-rational-tangent-cotangent-duality] identifies $T_{N/k,e}$ with $(\mathfrak m_e/\mathfrak m_e^2)^\vee$, which is therefore zero; this is $\operatorname{Lie}(N)$ in the sense of [lem-sfb-smooth-subgroup-tangent-generation]. Apply that node to the smooth connected affine group $G=N$, the empty finite family of smooth connected subgroups, and its trivial closed subgroup $K=1$. The empty family spans the zero tangent space, so that statement gives $N=1$. Since $N$ was an arbitrary smooth connected normal unipotent closed subgroup of $H$, this proves reductivity by its stated definition. The argument covers $H=1$, $T=1$, and $\Psi=\varnothing$.
